title: A New AI Tool From Google DeepMind Proved the Signal Protocol Is Secure
gist: Google DeepMind used a new agentic AI framework, AlphaProof Code, to formally verify key cryptographic guarantees of the Signal protocol in four weeks, finding no new flaws but correctly flagging known bugs in older versions. The open question is whether AI-automated formal verification can scale to whole codebases at workable cost; Google declined to disclose cost or commercial plans.

insights.claim: Google DeepMind used agentic AI via a new framework called AlphaProof Code to formally verify a number of the Signal protocol's key cryptographic guarantees in a four-week proof-of-concept project.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: Demonstrates AI can compress the slowest part of formal verification, a potential new product category in software security.
insights.locator: Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI

insights.claim: AlphaProof Code found no new vulnerabilities in the Signal protocol portions it analyzed, but when run on older Signal versions with known, long-fixed vulnerabilities it correctly identified them and showed those versions could not be formally verified.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: Validation against known bugs gives credibility to the tool as a real assurance method, not just a proof generator.
insights.locator: The DeepMind analysis did not find any new vulnerabilities

insights.claim: The DeepMind analysis further validates the cryptography protecting communications on the Signal app, Google Messages and WhatsApp, though it did not verify the entire Signal mobile app and benefited from Signal Foundation's prior formal verification work.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: Scope was limited and had a head start, so the four-week timeline may overstate how fast greenfield verification would be.
insights.locator: While the speed of the project was notable

insights.claim: Signal CTO Ehren Kret says DeepMind's approach enables significant expansion beyond prior formal verification of smaller code portions, increasing confidence as AI-driven security threats grow.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: Defensive AI verification is being framed as a response to offensive AI threats, a narrative supporting security spend.
insights.quote: As AI-driven security threats grow, rigorously verifying the Signal protocol implementation gives us even greater confidence in our code's privacy guarantees.
insights.locator: “While prior formal verification focused on smaller portions

insights.claim: Formal verification—using math to prove software behaves as intended with no critical vulnerabilities—has long been considered a holy grail of software security but was historically extremely time-consuming; agentic AI can significantly cut the time needed to develop the proofs.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: If proof generation becomes cheap, formal guarantees could move from niche (crypto protocols) to mainstream critical software.
insights.locator: Before the AI era, it was incredibly time-consuming

insights.claim: DeepMind researchers say a key advance is a human-AI collaboration process in which agents contribute and self-correct at almost every phase while humans review key junctures, rather than letting AI write both the goals and the proofs.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: Human-in-the-loop specification is positioned as the guard against AI self-grading, a design pattern to watch in AI assurance products.
insights.quote: We don’t want this sort of vibe world where AI is generating the goals and AI is generating the proofs and basically taking tests that are self-written,
insights.locator: The researchers say that some of their crucial advancements

insights.claim: The open question across the tech sector is whether AI-automated formal verification can scale to large codebases and entire software supply chains at a workable cost.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: Cost-per-verified-line is the key metric that will determine whether this becomes a commercial market.
insights.locator: The open question across the tech sector

insights.claim: Google conducted the Signal analysis free as a research project, declined to share its cost, and declined to say whether it plans a commercial formal verification product or service.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: Watch for a Google Cloud formal-verification offering; economics remain undisclosed.
insights.locator: DeepMind conducted the Signal analysis free of charge

insights.claim: Google Cloud chief scientist Pushmeet Kohli envisions banks and other assurance-dependent companies using AI formal verification to prove properties of their code.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: Financial services and regulated industries are the targeted early market for provable software assurance.
insights.quote: You can imagine banks, imagine all those other companies who rely on assurances and who worry about bugs who could now say, ‘I can prove these properties.’
insights.locator: For critical services used in high-stakes settings

insights.claim: DeepMind research scientist Swarat Chaudhuri says there is a long distance to go before AI formal verification can scale to all the world's software, which DeepMind aims to do.
insights.speaker: Lily Hay Newman
insights.so_what: DeepMind frames this as a long-horizon ambition; near-term impact likely limited to high-value components.
insights.quote: there is a long distance to go before we are able to scale this to all the software of the world
insights.locator: “We are very excited by this result
